```{r setup}
library(tidyWaste)
```

## Overview

**tidyWaste** is a meta-package: it installs and loads a family of packages
for environmental analysis in waste-management operations. A single
`library(tidyWaste)` attaches every core member, so you can move between
water-quality and meteorological work without juggling `library()` calls.

## The members

| Package | Domain | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [hydroSense](https://github.com/vorpalvorpal/hydroSense) | Water quality | Leachate-mixing fraction (end-member mixing), Bayesian imputation of below-detection analytes, and SSD-based toxicity (PAF / msPAF) for leachate-impacted freshwaters. |
| [meteoHazard](https://github.com/vorpalvorpal/meteoHazard) | Meteorology | Management-relevant hazard predictions: Thermal Work Limit (TWL) heat stress, plus odour-dispersion, wind-blown-litter and dust predictors. |

The family is expected to grow; new members are added to this meta-package as
they stabilise.

## Loading the family

```{r}
library(tidyWaste)
#> ── Attaching tidyWaste 0.0.0.9000 ──────────────────────────────────
#> ✔ hydroSense   0.2.0     ✔ meteoHazard   0.1.0
```

List the members at any time:

```{r}
tidyWaste_packages()
```

## Keeping up to date

`tidyWaste_update()` reports the installed version of each member and prints
the command to reinstall the latest from GitHub:

```{r}
tidyWaste_update()
```

## Name conflicts

As the family grows, two members may export functions of the same name. The
one that wins depends on attach order. `tidyWaste_conflicts()` surfaces these
so you can qualify the call explicitly (e.g. `hydroSense::foo()`):

```{r}
tidyWaste_conflicts()
```

## Where shared code lives

This meta-package sits at the *top* of the dependency graph: it imports the
members, so it can offer family-level conveniences but cannot host code that
the members themselves need. Shared building blocks — a common site object,
units and coordinate conventions, validation helpers and example data — belong
in a lower-level package that each member imports, not here.
